Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: incident fired -> high-inference-latency-prod (trigger: router_p50 > 600ms)
Alex: acked — I'm on it, looking at the grafana panel now https://grafana.internal/r/abcd
Sara: I see a tiny correlated spike on router CPU and a KV warmup pattern on the serving nodes, looks like short-lived KV cache churn at 16:03:02
Alex: hmm, error budget alerting too aggressively? this is only ~18s of elevated p50. open to silencing if it's noise.
PagerDuty Bot: auto-escalation scheduled in 2m to Maya if not acknowledged by rotation lead
Devon: I'll grab logs from the runtime, running the quick query:
```
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=redwood-serving --since=2m | grep "KV cache miss" | wc -l
```
Devon: got ~120 misses across the pool, but requests recovered immediately after.
Maya: ping — oncall handoff in 4m, leaving notes. Do we have customer impact?
Alex: quick check on customer-facing errors: 5xxs are flat, only latency. Most impacted requests were batched long tails from a couple of heavy prompts; no SRE alerts from rate-limiter.
Sara: looks like a synthetic canary run triggered longer sequences at once, caused kv cold paths to briefly surface. I can see the canary id in the logs: `canary-2026-03-15-16-02`
Alex: ok, let's squash the noise. I'll silence the PD rule for 10m and post a follow-up to tune the alert duration.
Alex: (silence command)
```
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Token xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://internal.alerts/api/v1/silence \
  -d '{"alert":"high-inference-latency-prod","duration_minutes":10,"reason":"transient canary-induced kv warmup, no customer impact"}'
```
PagerDuty Bot: silence applied to service high-inference-latency-prod for 10m by Alex :thumbsup:
Incident Bot: incident auto-resolved (duration 00:00:38) — PD incident cleared
Maya: thanks, Alex. I'll take the handoff — creating a short post-incident note and a ticket for tuning.
Maya: filing follow-up: TICKET-2456 (alert: increase min_firing_duration to 60s, add canary tag exclusion, and add KV warmup warmup-metric to suppression rules)
Sara: suggestion: add a short debounce in the routing layer to absorb synthetic bursts (batch smoothing) — I'll draft a proposal.
Devon: also adding a small KV pre-warm hook for known canary runs, we can gate it behind canary metadata.
Alex: agreed. No customer escalations, no rollback, just noise. We'll monitor next 24h and revisit if it recurs.
Maya: note for on-call board: if we see repeated sub-1m spikes, escalate to infra to raise the alert threshold.
Alex: adding a quick runbook snippet to the thread for next person:
```
Runbook: transient-latency-noise
1) Check grafana panel: router p50/p95, grouped by region
2) Check logs for canary id: grep "canary-"
3) If spike < 60s and no 5xxs, apply 10m silence with reason "transient canary noise"
4) Create follow-up ticket and tag as "alert-tuning"
```
Maya: leaving this unassigned for now, I'll include the canary owners on the follow-up and set a reminder for postmortem if repeats happen. :calendar:
Alex: :white_check_mark: closing thread, incident auto-resolved cleanly.
